metaTitle: SEO Agency in Melbourne: When Offshore Makes Sense
metaDescription: Melbourne SEO retainers run AUD 3,000-5,000 a month. We explain when an offshore team beats that, when it plainly doesn't, and what we charge.
answer: Melbourne SEO retainers commonly quote between AUD 3,000 and AUD 5,000 a month. That money is well spent locally when your growth depends on the map pack, local PR and relationships built over years. An offshore team like ours earns its place on content, technical work and national organic — not on handshakes in Richmond.
takeaways: **AUD 3,000–5,000/mo** in Melbourne mostly buys senior Australian time. If the work genuinely needs senior Australian time, pay for it.
Trades and clinics live in the map pack, where proximity to the searcher outranks almost everything a remote team can do.
`.com.au` needs an Australian presence to register. Hosting location barely matters. Agencies conflate those two questions constantly.
Our guarantee is movement against **your own** frozen 90-day baseline — never a promised position. That reads identically in AUD and INR.

sections.h2: What AUD 3,000–5,000 a month actually buys here
body: Australian SEO pricing is unusually consistent for a market this size. Small local campaigns quote around AUD 1,500–2,500 a month, the mid-market sits at AUD 3,000–5,000, and anything genuinely contested — national e-commerce, insurance, personal injury — starts above that. Treat those bands as the shape of the market, not a price list; they move.

The reason those numbers look steep next to an Indian or Filipino quote is not margin. It's payroll. A senior Australian SEO specialist costs a multiple of an equally senior Indian one, and a Melbourne agency carries superannuation at 12%, Victorian payroll tax above the threshold, four weeks of leave, and rent in the CBD or somewhere in the inner north pretending not to be the CBD.

callout.title: The question that reprices the room
callout.body: Ask any Melbourne agency what share of your retainer is senior Australian time versus junior or offshore time. A meaningful number of Australian agencies already subcontract delivery to teams in India or the Philippines and invoice at Melbourne rates. That's legal and often perfectly fine — but you should know whether you're buying the local team or just the local invoice.

sections.h2: When you genuinely need someone in Melbourne
body: This is the section most agency location pages leave out. There are Melbourne briefs we turn down, and they tend to look like this.
bullets: **Your growth runs on local press.** If the plan involves The Age, Broadsheet or a Herald Sun business page, you want someone who already knows those desks. Cold outreach from an Indian inbox to a Melbourne newsroom converts badly, and pretending otherwise burns your money and our reputation.

**Your links come from memberships and sponsorships.** Master Builders Victoria, the VACC, your council's business directory, the netball club whose jerseys carry your logo. Those links exist because someone in your industry knows you. An agency can chase them; it can't manufacture the relationship.
**Someone has to walk the site.** Multi-site retail, a showroom, a fit-out. Store photography, on-site audits, training counter staff to ask for reviews — that's physical work.

**You need people on Melbourne morning time, daily.** Melbourne runs four and a half to five and a half hours ahead of India. A 3pm Melbourne call is 9:30am in Bengaluru — a real overlap, and we use it. An 8am stand-up is 2:30am, and anyone promising to take that one daily is lying to at least one of us.
**You're in a regulated health category and want local legal cover.** See the callout below.

sections.h2: Trades, clinics and franchises: the map pack is the whole game
body: Three Melbourne categories dominate local search competition, and each breaks differently.

Trades — plumbers, sparkies, builders, arborists — compete almost entirely inside the local pack on suburb-level queries. Proximity to the searcher is the heaviest signal Google applies, which is why a mediocre Brunswick electrician beats an excellent Frankston one for a Brunswick search. What you can control is category selection, review velocity, service-area configuration, and whether your suburb pages say anything a human wrote.
Clinics — dental, physio, cosmetic, allied health — face identical pack maths plus an advertising regulator, which changes the review playbook that works everywhere else.

Franchise groups have the hardest version. Forty near-identical location pages is a duplication problem before it's a ranking problem, and franchise SEO is mostly governance: who owns the profile, who answers reviews, who stops the Ballarat franchisee buying links on the group's domain.

callout.title: Ahpra changes the review playbook
callout.body: Australia's National Law restricts the use of testimonials in advertising a regulated health service. Ahpra's guidance treats reviews you solicit and control differently from unsolicited reviews on a platform you don't. Exactly where your practice sits is a question for your lawyer and your practice manager — not for an SEO agency, and certainly not for one that has never read the guidance. We'd rather say that than guess on your registration.

sections.h2: com.au, hosting and whether you need an Australian entity
body: Three questions get tangled together in nearly every Melbourne pitch. They are separate questions with separate answers.

`.com.au` requires an Australian presence to register — an ABN, an ACN or an Australian trade mark — under auDA policy. Since 2022 you can also register a direct `.au`. Because it's a country-code domain, it geo-targets Australia clearly and permanently.

That's an advantage if you're Australia-only for the foreseeable future, and a ceiling if you later want Singapore or Auckland. Australia-only: take the `.com.au`. Anything else: take the `.com` and build country folders.

Server location is close to irrelevant as a ranking signal, especially behind a country-code domain or a CDN. It still matters for latency, and latency shows up in Core Web Vitals. Choose the fast option, not the patriotic one.

You do not need an Australian company to rank in Australia. You do need a genuine Australian address and phone number to hold a Google Business Profile for a Melbourne location, and verification is stricter than it was five years ago. If you have no real presence in Victoria, don't invent one — Google is unforgiving on address problems and reinstatement can take months you don't have.

sections.h2: What we're actually good at from this distance
body: Strip out everything that needs a Melbourne postcode and a surprising amount remains — usually the part that's been quietly neglected while everyone argued about the map pack.
bullets: **Technical.** Crawling, indexing, Core Web Vitals, schema, migrations. None of it cares where the person typing sits.
**Content at volume.** Suburb pages that aren't spun, service pages that answer the question a buyer actually typed, comparison content that catches people earlier than your competitors do.

**Programmatic and e-commerce.** Faceted navigation, category architecture, thousands of URLs kept out of trouble. This is where an Indian cost base buys you more work per dollar rather than the same work cheaper.
**National organic rather than local.** If you sell Australia-wide, the pack matters far less than the fact that you have twelve pages and the market leader has four hundred.

sections.h2: How the guarantee reads in AUD
body: We don't promise you a position. Nobody controls Google's index, and an agency promising a number-one for a Melbourne commercial term is either guessing or planning to buy links with your domain name attached to them.

What we do instead: on day one we freeze your trailing-90-day count of qualified leads from organic search. Not sessions, not average position — leads, in your CRM, attributed to organic. If we haven't beaten that number within 90 days, we keep working free until we do.

Currency changes none of the mechanics and all of the stakes. Our SEO starts at ₹75,000 a month ex-GST, smaller sites from ₹40,000 — convert on the day you sign, because the rupee moves and we won't pretend otherwise. See [our pricing in full](/pricing) and [how the SEO engagement runs](/seo). If the work is genuinely map-pack-first, read [what a local SEO programme costs](/cost/local-seo-cost) first.
It's also why we cap ourselves at three new clients a month. You can't carry that downside at volume, and any agency offering the same promise to fifty accounts hasn't done the arithmetic.

faqs.q: How much does SEO cost in Melbourne?
faqs.a: Small local campaigns quote around AUD 1,500–2,500 a month, mid-market work sits at AUD 3,000–5,000, and competitive national or regulated categories start above AUD 6,000. The gap versus offshore pricing is almost entirely Australian salaries, superannuation and payroll tax rather than margin.

faqs.q: Do I need a .com.au domain to rank in Australia?
faqs.a: No, but it helps if you're Australia-only. A .com.au geo-targets Australia permanently and requires an Australian presence — an ABN, ACN or Australian trade mark — to register. If you plan to sell into New Zealand or Asia later, a .com with country folders avoids repainting yourself into a corner.

faqs.q: Can an offshore agency rank a Melbourne business in the map pack?
faqs.a: Partly. Profile optimisation, categories, service areas, review systems and suburb landing pages all work remotely. What doesn't travel is local press, sponsorships, industry-body links and anyone physically visiting your locations. If the pack is your entire growth plan, hire locally.

faqs.q: What hours would an India-based team work for a Melbourne client?
faqs.a: Melbourne is four and a half to five and a half hours ahead of India depending on daylight saving. The workable overlap is Melbourne afternoon against Indian morning — a 3pm Melbourne call is 9:30am in Bengaluru. Daily 8am Melbourne meetings aren't realistic and we'd say so before you signed.

faqs.q: Do you guarantee first-page rankings in Melbourne?
faqs.a: No, and neither should anyone else. We guarantee movement against your own baseline: your trailing-90-day qualified leads from organic, frozen on day one. Miss it in 90 days and we keep working free until we beat it. A promised position is a promise about someone else's algorithm.
